equivalents.ContourWithBarriers: How contouring works' contours drawn on each side of the barriers apart (Esri's How contouring works; the barriers as Terzopoulos 1988 treats discontinuities)
equivalents.Kriging: ordinary and universal kriging with a semivariogram fitted by weighted least squares (Cressie 1985; Cressie 1993, §3.2–3.4; Johnston et al. 2001, Appendix A)
equivalents.ObserverPoints: Viewshed's R3 line of sight for each observer, its visibility encoded as the bitwise OR of each observer's bit (Franklin and Ray 1994; the observer bits of How Geodesic Viewshed works; the OBSn fields of Using Viewshed and Observer Points for visibility)
equivalents.RegularizeAdjacentBuildingFootprint: shared-arc Douglas–Peucker simplification with each edge turned to the group's dominant orientation, shared vertices placed once for every footprint that uses them (Douglas and Peucker 1973, The Canadian Cartographer 10(2); Duchêne, Bard, Barillot, Ruas, Trévisan and Holzapfel 2003, 5th ICA Workshop on Progress in Automated Map Generalisation; Kåsa 1976, IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement 25(1))
equivalents.RegularizeBuildingFootprint: Douglas–Peucker simplification with each edge turned to the dominant orientation, its right angles or diagonals, or Kåsa's least-squares circle (Douglas and Peucker 1973, The Canadian Cartographer 10(2); Duchêne, Bard, Barillot, Ruas, Trévisan and Holzapfel 2003, 5th ICA Workshop on Progress in Automated Map Generalisation; Kåsa 1976, IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement 25(1))
equivalents.Spline: the regularized spline and the spline with tension (Mitas and Mitasova 1988; Franke 1982)
equivalents.SplineWithBarriers: minimum curvature — the surface minimising the summed squared discrete Laplacian, solved directly — with the barriers cutting the stencil (Briggs 1974, Geophysics 39; Terzopoulos 1988, IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 10(4))
equivalents.SunShadowVolume: the swept shadow volume: the union of each face's prism along the light rays (Crow 1977; sun position NOAA / Meeus 1998)
equivalents.SurfaceParameters: a quadratic (Evans 1980; Wood 1996) or biquadratic (Zevenbergen and Thorne 1987) surface fitted by least squares over the neighbourhood, with slope, aspect and the curvatures of Minár, Evans and Jenčo 2020 (Wood 1996, PhD thesis, University of Leicester; Zevenbergen and Thorne 1987, Earth Surface Processes and Landforms 12; Minár, Evans and Jenčo 2020, Earth-Science Reviews 211, 103414)
equivalents.TopoToRaster: ANUDEM's locally adaptive thin plate fit at successively finer resolutions with drainage enforcement by descending chains through the lowest saddle (Hutchinson 1989, Journal of Hydrology 106; Hutchinson, Stein, Stein and Xu 2009, MODSIM §2.1; Hutchinson, Xu and Stein 2011, Geomorphometry; Barnes, Lehman and Mulla 2014, Computers & Geosciences 62)
equivalents.TopoToRasterByFile: ANUDEM's locally adaptive thin plate fit at successively finer resolutions with drainage enforcement by descending chains through the lowest saddle (Hutchinson 1989, Journal of Hydrology 106; Hutchinson, Stein, Stein and Xu 2009, MODSIM §2.1; Hutchinson, Xu and Stein 2011, Geomorphometry; Barnes, Lehman and Mulla 2014, Computers & Geosciences 62)
equivalents.Viewshed: R3 line-of-sight viewshed (Franklin and Ray 1994; How Viewshed works)
equivalents.Viewshed2: the geodesic sight line: surface and observers in 3D geocentric coordinates, the ground path divided into cell-size steps, the surface by inverse distance weighting (How Geodesic Viewshed works; Bowring 1976, Survey Review 23; the refraction term of How Viewshed works)

equivalents.AnalyzeChangesUsingLandTrendr: LandTrendr temporal segmentation: despiking, vertex search by largest departure, culling by angle, continuous piecewise-linear least squares and selection by the F-test's p-value (Kennedy, Yang and Cohen 2010, Remote Sensing of Environment 114, 2897–2910)
equivalents.ApplyComplexDataFilter: Goldstein-Werner adaptive spectral filter on overlapping patches (Goldstein and Werner, Geophys. Res. Lett. 25(21) 1998)
equivalents.ApplyCoregistration: geometric coregistration through orbits and a DEM, bilinear resampling of the secondary (Sansosti et al., IEEE TGRS 44(8) 2006)
equivalents.ApplyGeometricTerrainCorrection: range-Doppler terrain correction onto a WGS 84 grid, bilinear resampling (Small and Schubert, Guide to ASAR Geocoding, ESA RSL-ASAR-GC-AD, 2008)
equivalents.ApplyRadiometricTerrainFlattening: area-based radiometric terrain flattening: DEM facets projected into radar geometry (Small, IEEE TGRS 49(8) 2011)
equivalents.Classify: the classifier definition's own rule: Gaussian maximum likelihood, nearest isodata mean, k-nearest neighbours or one-against-one linear support vector machines, as the Train tool wrote it (Richards and Jia 2006, §8.3; Ball and Hall 1965; Cover and Hart 1967; Cortes and Vapnik 1995)
equivalents.ClassifyRaster: the classifier definition's own rule: Gaussian maximum likelihood, nearest isodata mean, k-nearest neighbours or one-against-one linear support vector machines, as the Train tool wrote it (Richards and Jia 2006, §8.3; Ball and Hall 1965; Cover and Hart 1967; Cortes and Vapnik 1995)
equivalents.ColorspaceConversion: Smith's hexcone RGB↔HSV, hue rescaled to 0–240 and saturation and value to 0–255 as the Color Model Conversion page gives them (Smith, Color Gamut Transform Pairs, SIGGRAPH '78, 1978)
equivalents.ComputeCoherence: boxcar sample coherence |Σ s1 s2*| / sqrt(Σ|s1|² Σ|s2|²) (Touzi et al., IEEE TGRS 37(1) 1999; Hanssen, Radar Interferometry, 2001, §4.4)
equivalents.ComputeSARIndices: RVI 8σHV/(σHH+σVV+2σHV) quad and 4σx/(σco+σx) dual; RFDI (σco−σx)/(σco+σx); CSI (σHH−σVV)/(σHH+σVV) (Kim and van Zyl, IEEE TGRS 47(8) 2009; Mitchard et al., Biogeosciences 9 2012; Pope et al., RSE 48 1994)
equivalents.ComputeSegmentAttributes: compactness as area over the area of the smallest enclosing circle, rectangularity as area over the area of the minimum rotated bounding rectangle (MacEachren 1985, Geografiska Annaler 67B(1); Rosin 1999, Machine Vision and Applications 11)
equivalents.Deburst: bursts joined at the middle of each overlap, invalid samples blanked (ESA Sentinel-1 Product Specification S1-RS-MDA-52-7441, burst layout)
equivalents.Despeckle: Lee (1980), Refined Lee (Lee 1981), Enhanced Lee and Gamma-MAP (Lopes et al. 1990), Frost (1982) and Kuan (1985) local-statistics filters (Lee, IEEE PAMI 2(2) 1980; Lee, CGIP 17 1981; Lopes, Touzi and Nezry, IEEE TGRS 28(6) 1990; Frost et al., IEEE PAMI 4(2) 1982; Kuan et al., IEEE PAMI 7(2) 1985)
equivalents.DetectBrightOceanObjects: two-parameter CFAR over a background ring, then connected components measured by their minimum rotated rectangle (Crisp, The State-of-the-Art in Ship Detection in SAR Imagery, DSTO-RR-0272, 2004)
equivalents.DetectDarkOceanAreas: adaptive threshold below the local mean, then connected components (Solberg et al., IEEE TGRS 37(4) 1999)
equivalents.ElevationVoidFill: inverse distance weighting (power 2) from the cells bordering each void (Shepard, Proc. 23rd ACM National Conference, 1968)
equivalents.ExtractOceanWinds: wind direction from the image's streaks by the local gradient method and wind speed by inverting CMOD5.N (Koch, IEEE TGRS 42(4) 2004; Hersbach, CMOD5.N, ECMWF Tech. Memo. 554, 2008)
equivalents.GenerateInterferogram: s1 s2* with the phase of the reference geometry, 4π(R2 − R1)/λ on the ellipsoid or DEM, removed (Hanssen, Radar Interferometry, 2001, §2.4)
equivalents.GenerateRadiometricTerrainCorrectedData: the RTC chain of grapy's own SAR tools: thermal noise, beta nought, deburst, multilook, Small (2011) flattening, Refined Lee, range-Doppler terrain correction (ADR-237)
equivalents.GenerateTrend: least-squares linear, polynomial and harmonic trends, and the Mann-Kendall and Seasonal-Kendall tests (ordinary least squares (Draper and Smith 1998, Applied Regression Analysis, ch. 5); harmonic regression after Zhu and Woodcock 2014, Remote Sensing of Environment 144; Mann 1945, Econometrica 13(3); Kendall 1975, Rank Correlation Methods; Sen 1968, JASA 63(324); Hirsch, Slack and Smith 1982, Water Resources Research 18(1))
equivalents.GenerateTrendRaster: least-squares linear, polynomial and harmonic trends, and the Mann-Kendall and Seasonal-Kendall tests (ordinary least squares (Draper and Smith 1998, Applied Regression Analysis, ch. 5); harmonic regression after Zhu and Woodcock 2014, Remote Sensing of Environment 144; Mann 1945, Econometrica 13(3); Kendall 1975, Rank Correlation Methods; Sen 1968, JASA 63(324); Hirsch, Slack and Smith 1982, Water Resources Research 18(1))
equivalents.InspectTrainingSamples: each training sample's share of cells the classifier definition classifies as its class (the accuracy score of Inspect Training Samples' page (correct cells over the sample's cells), with the classifier definition's own rule)
equivalents.InterpolateFromSpatiotemporalPoints: inverse distance, nearest neighbour, cell mean and median, linear interpolation on a Delaunay triangulation and Sibson's natural neighbours, for each period's points (Shepard 1968, Proc. 23rd ACM National Conference; Delaunay 1934; Sibson 1981, in Interpreting Multivariate Data, pp. 21-36)
equivalents.LinearUnmixing: least squares unmixing: unconstrained, sum-to-one by Lagrange multiplier, non-negative by Lawson-Hanson NNLS, both by fully constrained least squares (Keshava and Mustard, IEEE Signal Processing Magazine 19(1) 2002; Lawson and Hanson, Solving Least Squares Problems, 1974, ch. 23; Heinz and Chang, IEEE TGRS 39(3) 2001)
equivalents.MLClassify: Gaussian maximum likelihood classification with equal priors (Richards and Jia 2006, Remote Sensing Digital Image Analysis, 4th ed., §8.3)
equivalents.Merge: mosaic of rasters by local operations over the valid inputs (Tomlin 1990, Geographic Information Systems and Cartographic Modeling, ch. 3 (local operations))
equivalents.MultidimensionalPrincipalComponents: principal components of the slices' covariance matrix (Jolliffe 2002, Principal Component Analysis, ch. 1)
equivalents.MultidimensionalRasterCorrelation: Pearson, Spearman and Kendall correlations with their standard significance tests (Pearson 1896; Spearman 1904; Kendall 1938, Biometrika 30; Sheskin 2011, Handbook of Parametric and Nonparametric Statistical Procedures, tests 28 and 30)
equivalents.Pansharpen: Brovey, Esri, simple mean and IHS fusion as Fundamentals of pan sharpening writes them, and Gram-Schmidt spectral sharpening (Esri, Fundamentals of pan sharpening; Laben and Brower 2000, US Patent 6,011,875; Tu et al. 2001, Information Fusion 2(3) (the additive IHS))
equivalents.Percentile: sample quantiles: nearest rank (type 1) and linear interpolation (type 7) (Hyndman and Fan 1996, The American Statistician 50(4))
equivalents.PredictUsingTrend: the fitted least-squares trend evaluated at the new dimension values (ordinary least squares (Draper and Smith 1998, Applied Regression Analysis, ch. 5); harmonic regression after Zhu and Woodcock 2014, Remote Sensing of Environment 144; Mann 1945, Econometrica 13(3); Kendall 1975, Rank Correlation Methods; Sen 1968, JASA 63(324); Hirsch, Slack and Smith 1982, Water Resources Research 18(1))
equivalents.PredictUsingTrendRaster: the fitted least-squares trend evaluated at the new dimension values (ordinary least squares (Draper and Smith 1998, Applied Regression Analysis, ch. 5); harmonic regression after Zhu and Woodcock 2014, Remote Sensing of Environment 144; Mann 1945, Econometrica 13(3); Kendall 1975, Rank Correlation Methods; Sen 1968, JASA 63(324); Hirsch, Slack and Smith 1982, Water Resources Research 18(1))
equivalents.RegionGrow: seeded region growing from each seed point, within its radius and spectral threshold (Adams and Bischof 1994, IEEE Trans. Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 16(6))
equivalents.RemoveRasterSegmentTilingArtifacts: segments cut by a tile seam merged when their common boundary lies wholly on the seam and their colours agree within the default spectral radius (Comaniciu and Meer 2002 §4.2's range bandwidth applied across the seams Segment Mean Shift's page says its tiled processing leaves)
equivalents.Resample: nearest neighbour, bilinear and Keys cubic convolution (a = −0.5) on cell centres; majority over the 4×4 nearest centres; average, minimum and maximum over the input cells whose centres the output cell covers (Keys, IEEE TASSP 29(6) 1981; Parker, Kenyon and Troxel, IEEE TMI 2(1) 1983)
equivalents.S1ThermalNoiseRemoval: RemoveThermalNoise's denoising on every band (ESA MPC-0392)
equivalents.SegMeanShift: mean shift filtering in the joint spatial-range domain with a flat kernel, region delineation and small-region merging (Comaniciu and Meer 2002, IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 24(5), §4.1-4.2)
equivalents.SegmentMeanShift: mean shift filtering in the joint spatial-range domain with a flat kernel, region delineation and small-region merging (Comaniciu and Meer 2002, IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 24(5), §4.1-4.2)
equivalents.Speckle: Lee (1980), Enhanced Lee and Gamma-MAP (Lopes et al. 1990), Frost (1982), Kuan (1985) and Refined Lee (Lee 1981) local-statistics filters, as arcpy.ia.Despeckle builds them (Lee, IEEE PAMI 2(2) 1980; Lee, CGIP 17 1981; Lopes, Touzi and Nezry, IEEE TGRS 28(6) 1990; Frost et al., IEEE PAMI 4(2) 1982; Kuan et al., IEEE PAMI 7(2) 1985)
equivalents.Stretch: a linear contrast stretch to 0–255 (Richards and Jia, Remote Sensing Digital Image Analysis, 4th ed., §4.3)
equivalents.Threshold: Otsu's threshold on a 256-bin histogram (Otsu 1979, IEEE Trans. Systems, Man and Cybernetics 9(1))
equivalents.TrainIsoClusterClassifier: isodata clustering: migrating means with cluster elimination and merging (Ball and Hall 1965, ISODATA, Stanford Research Institute; Tou and Gonzalez 1974, Pattern Recognition Principles, §3.3.6; How Iso Cluster works)
equivalents.TrainKNearestNeighborClassifier: k-nearest-neighbour plurality vote by Euclidean distance (Cover and Hart 1967, IEEE Trans. Information Theory 13(1))
equivalents.TrainMaximumLikelihoodClassifier: Gaussian maximum likelihood classification with equal priors (Richards and Jia 2006, Remote Sensing Digital Image Analysis, 4th ed., §8.3)
equivalents.TrainSupportVectorMachineClassifier: one-against-one linear soft-margin support vector machines (C = 1) on standardised attributes, trained by sequential minimal optimisation (Cortes and Vapnik 1995, Machine Learning 20(3); Platt 1998, MSR-TR-98-14; Hsu and Lin 2002, IEEE Trans. Neural Networks 13(2))
equivalents.TrendToRGB: slope and intercept, or harmonic amplitude and phase through HSV, stretched linearly to 0–255 (Smith 1978, Color gamut transform pairs, SIGGRAPH '78; the Trend to RGB function's description)
equivalents.UnwrapPhase: weighted least-squares unwrapping by preconditioned conjugate gradient, DCT preconditioner (Ghiglia and Romero, J. Opt. Soc. Am. A 11(1) 1994; Ghiglia and Pritt, Two-Dimensional Phase Unwrapping, 1998)

equivalents.DarcyVelocity: finite-difference Darcy seepage velocity (Darcy's law on a finite-difference grid with harmonic-mean face transmissivity, as How Darcy Flow and Darcy Velocity work writes it; Anderson, Woessner and Hunt 2015, Applied Groundwater Modeling, ch. 3)
equivalents.DistanceAccumulation: fast marching surface reconstruction, eight network estimates and four Eikonal steps per cell, the direction-dependent slope solved again along each step's own gradient (Sethian 1999, Level Set Methods and Fast Marching Methods, as Distance accumulation algorithm cites it)
equivalents.DistanceAllocation: fast marching surface reconstruction, eight network estimates and four Eikonal steps per cell, the direction-dependent slope solved again along each step's own gradient (Sethian 1999, Level Set Methods and Fast Marching Methods, as Distance accumulation algorithm cites it)
equivalents.EditSignatures: merged signatures by the pooled mean and covariance of their classes' cells (Chan, Golub and LeVeque 1979, Updating formulae and a pairwise algorithm for computing sample variances, Stanford CS-79-773; How Dendrogram works (pooled statistics of a merged class))
equivalents.ElevationVoidFill: inverse distance weighting (power 2) from the cells bordering each void (Shepard, Proc. 23rd ACM National Conference, 1968)
equivalents.Expand: zone growth by morphological dilation, or by Euclidean distance (Serra 1982, Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology, ch. 2; Danielsson 1980, Computer Graphics and Image Processing 14)
equivalents.Filter: 3 × 3 low-pass (mean) and high-pass (Laplacian, centre 8) filters (Gonzalez and Woods, Digital Image Processing, 3rd ed., §3.5–3.6)
equivalents.FuzzyMembership: the fuzzy membership functions in the forms of Esri's transformation-function formulas (Esri, Formulas for the transformation functions (Spatial Analyst reference), which give the same shapes as text; hedges after Zadeh 1972, A fuzzy-set-theoretic interpretation of linguistic hedges)
equivalents.InspectTrainingSamples: each training sample's share of cells the classifier definition classifies as its class (the accuracy score of Inspect Training Samples' page (correct cells over the sample's cells), with the classifier definition's own rule)
equivalents.KernelDensity: the quartic (biweight) kernel density estimate with Silverman's rule-of-thumb bandwidth (Silverman 1986, Density Estimation for Statistics and Data Analysis, eq. 4.5 and §3.4.2)
equivalents.Kriging: ordinary and universal kriging with a semivariogram fitted by weighted least squares (Cressie 1985, Mathematical Geology 17(5); Cressie 1993, Statistics for Spatial Data, §3.2–3.4; models of Johnston et al. 2001, Using ArcGIS Geostatistical Analyst, Appendix A)
equivalents.LinearUnmixing: least squares unmixing: unconstrained, sum-to-one by Lagrange multiplier, non-negative by Lawson-Hanson NNLS, both by fully constrained least squares (Keshava and Mustard, IEEE Signal Processing Magazine 19(1) 2002; Lawson and Hanson, Solving Least Squares Problems, 1974, ch. 23; Heinz and Chang, IEEE TGRS 39(3) 2001)
equivalents.MLClassify: Gaussian maximum likelihood classification with equal priors (Richards and Jia 2006, Remote Sensing Digital Image Analysis, 4th ed., §8.3)
equivalents.MajorityFilter: majority filtering with a contiguity test (the page's own replacement rule, with contiguity as connectedness in the neighbour ring (Rosenfeld 1970, Journal of the ACM 17(1)))
equivalents.Merge: mosaic of rasters by local operations over the valid inputs (Tomlin 1990, Geographic Information Systems and Cartographic Modeling, ch. 3 (local operations))
equivalents.NaturalNeighbor: Sibson's natural neighbour interpolation (Sibson 1981, in Interpreting Multivariate Data, pp. 21–36)
equivalents.Nibble: nearest-neighbour replacement by exact Euclidean distance (Danielsson 1980, Computer Graphics and Image Processing 14)
equivalents.ObserverPoints: Viewshed's R3 line of sight for each observer, its visibility encoded as the bitwise OR of each observer's bit (Franklin and Ray 1994; the observer bits of How Geodesic Viewshed works; the OBSn fields of Using Viewshed and Observer Points for visibility)
equivalents.OptimalPathAsLine: slopeline tracing down the back-direction raster across the lattice through the cell centres, as Distance accumulation algorithm draws it (Douglas 1994, Least-cost Path in GIS Using an Accumulated Cost Surface and Slopelines)
equivalents.OptimalPathAsRaster: slopeline tracing down the back-direction raster across the lattice through the cell centres, as Distance accumulation algorithm draws it (Douglas 1994, Least-cost Path in GIS Using an Accumulated Cost Surface and Slopelines)
equivalents.Pansharpen: Brovey, Esri, simple mean and IHS fusion as Fundamentals of pan sharpening writes them, and Gram-Schmidt spectral sharpening (Esri, Fundamentals of pan sharpening; Laben and Brower 2000, US Patent 6,011,875; Tu et al. 2001, Information Fusion 2(3) (the additive IHS))
equivalents.Percentile: sample quantiles: nearest rank (type 1) and linear interpolation (type 7) (Hyndman and Fan 1996, The American Statistician 50(4))
equivalents.PointsSolarRadiation: the hemispherical viewshed, sun map and sky map model of Fu and Rich, with the direct and diffuse equations of How solar radiation is calculated (Fu and Rich 2002, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture 37, 25–35; Rich et al. 1994, ASPRS Technical Papers, 524–529; Fu 2000, Ph.D. thesis, University of Kansas; Spencer 1971, Search 2(5); Kasten and Young 1989, Applied Optics 28(22))
equivalents.PrincipalComponents: principal components of the band covariance matrix (Jolliffe 2002, Principal Component Analysis, ch. 1)
equivalents.RasterSolarRadiation: the Fu and Rich direct and diffuse equations evaluated each half hour with the sun placed by NOAA's Solar Calculator for each block of cells (Fu and Rich 2002, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture 37; Rich et al. 1994, ASPRS Technical Papers; the sun's position by NOAA's Solar Calculator (Meeus 1998, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 25 and 28))
equivalents.RegionGrow: seeded region growing from each seed point, within its radius and spectral threshold (Adams and Bischof 1994, IEEE Trans. Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 16(6))
equivalents.RemoveRasterSegmentTilingArtifacts: segments cut by a tile seam merged when their common boundary lies wholly on the seam and their colours agree within the default spectral radius (Comaniciu and Meer 2002 §4.2's range bandwidth applied across the seams Segment Mean Shift's page says its tiled processing leaves)
equivalents.Resample: nearest neighbour, bilinear and Keys cubic convolution (a = −0.5) on cell centres; majority over the 4×4 nearest centres; average, minimum and maximum over the input cells whose centres the output cell covers (Keys, IEEE TASSP 29(6) 1981; Parker, Kenyon and Troxel, IEEE TMI 2(1) 1983)
equivalents.RescaleByFunction: linear rescaling of the transformed values onto the evaluation scale (the min-max normalisation of the transformed cells; the functions and their fitted defaults are Esri's Formulas for the transformation functions, given as text)
equivalents.SegMeanShift: mean shift filtering in the joint spatial-range domain with a flat kernel, region delineation and small-region merging (Comaniciu and Meer 2002, IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 24(5), §4.1-4.2)
equivalents.SegmentMeanShift: mean shift filtering in the joint spatial-range domain with a flat kernel, region delineation and small-region merging (Comaniciu and Meer 2002, IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 24(5), §4.1-4.2)
equivalents.Shrink: zone shrinking by morphological erosion (Serra 1982, Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology, ch. 2)
equivalents.SolarRadiationGraphics: the hemispherical viewshed, sun map and sky map model of Fu and Rich, with the direct and diffuse equations of How solar radiation is calculated (Fu and Rich 2002, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture 37, 25–35; Rich et al. 1994, ASPRS Technical Papers, 524–529; Fu 2000, Ph.D. thesis, University of Kansas; Spencer 1971, Search 2(5); Kasten and Young 1989, Applied Optics 28(22))
equivalents.Speckle: Lee (1980), Enhanced Lee and Gamma-MAP (Lopes et al. 1990), Frost (1982), Kuan (1985) and Refined Lee (Lee 1981) local-statistics filters, as arcpy.ia.Despeckle builds them (Lee, IEEE PAMI 2(2) 1980; Lee, CGIP 17 1981; Lopes, Touzi and Nezry, IEEE TGRS 28(6) 1990; Frost et al., IEEE PAMI 4(2) 1982; Kuan et al., IEEE PAMI 7(2) 1985)
equivalents.Spline: the regularized spline and the spline with tension (Mitas and Mitasova 1988, Mathematical Geology 20(8); Franke 1982, Computers and Mathematics with Applications 8(4); the page's own tension basis)
equivalents.SplineWithBarriers: minimum curvature — the surface minimising the summed squared discrete Laplacian, solved directly — with the barriers cutting the stencil (Briggs 1974, Geophysics 39; Terzopoulos 1988, IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 10(4))
equivalents.Stretch: a linear contrast stretch to 0–255 (Richards and Jia, Remote Sensing Digital Image Analysis, 4th ed., §4.3)
equivalents.SurfaceParameters: a quadratic (Evans 1980; Wood 1996) or biquadratic (Zevenbergen and Thorne 1987) surface fitted by least squares over the neighbourhood, with slope, aspect and the curvatures of Minár, Evans and Jenčo 2020 (Wood 1996, PhD thesis, University of Leicester; Zevenbergen and Thorne 1987, Earth Surface Processes and Landforms 12; Minár, Evans and Jenčo 2020, Earth-Science Reviews 211, 103414)
equivalents.Threshold: Otsu's threshold on a 256-bin histogram (Otsu 1979, IEEE Trans. Systems, Man and Cybernetics 9(1))
equivalents.TopoToRaster: ANUDEM's locally adaptive thin plate fit at successively finer resolutions with drainage enforcement by descending chains through the lowest saddle (Hutchinson 1989, Journal of Hydrology 106; Hutchinson, Stein, Stein and Xu 2009, MODSIM §2.1; Hutchinson, Xu and Stein 2011, Geomorphometry; Barnes, Lehman and Mulla 2014, Computers & Geosciences 62)
equivalents.TopoToRasterByFile: ANUDEM's locally adaptive thin plate fit at successively finer resolutions with drainage enforcement by descending chains through the lowest saddle (Hutchinson 1989, Journal of Hydrology 106; Hutchinson, Stein, Stein and Xu 2009, MODSIM §2.1; Hutchinson, Xu and Stein 2011, Geomorphometry; Barnes, Lehman and Mulla 2014, Computers & Geosciences 62)
equivalents.TrainIsoClusterClassifier: isodata clustering: migrating means with cluster elimination and merging (Ball and Hall 1965, ISODATA, Stanford Research Institute; Tou and Gonzalez 1974, Pattern Recognition Principles, §3.3.6; How Iso Cluster works)
equivalents.TrainKNearestNeighborClassifier: k-nearest-neighbour plurality vote by Euclidean distance (Cover and Hart 1967, IEEE Trans. Information Theory 13(1))
equivalents.TrainMaximumLikelihoodClassifier: Gaussian maximum likelihood classification with equal priors (Richards and Jia 2006, Remote Sensing Digital Image Analysis, 4th ed., §8.3)
equivalents.TrainSupportVectorMachineClassifier: one-against-one linear soft-margin support vector machines (C = 1) on standardised attributes, trained by sequential minimal optimisation (Cortes and Vapnik 1995, Machine Learning 20(3); Platt 1998, MSR-TR-98-14; Hsu and Lin 2002, IEEE Trans. Neural Networks 13(2))
equivalents.Viewshed: R3 line-of-sight viewshed (R3 line of sight with linear interpolation between cells (Franklin and Ray 1994, Higher isn't necessarily better), with the curvature and refraction correction and observer fields of How Viewshed works)
equivalents.Viewshed2: the geodesic sight line: surface and observers in 3D geocentric coordinates, the ground path divided into cell-size steps, the surface by inverse distance weighting (How Geodesic Viewshed works; Bowring 1976, Survey Review 23; the refraction term of How Viewshed works)
equivalents.Visibility: R3 line-of-sight visibility (R3 line of sight with linear interpolation between cells (Franklin and Ray 1994, Higher isn't necessarily better), with the curvature and refraction correction and observer fields of How Viewshed works)
equivalents.ZonalFill: each zone filled with the lowest weight on its boundary, the pour point of its watershed (Jenson and Domingue 1988, Photogrammetric Engineering and Remote Sensing 54(11))

equivalents.ColocationAnalysis: the local colocation quotient with a Gaussian, bisquare or box kernel and conditional permutation pseudo p-values with a stated seed; the global colocation quotient as their mean (Leslie and Kronenfeld 2011; Wang, Hu, Wang and Li 2017)

equivalents.GWR: geographically weighted regression with a Gaussian or bisquare kernel and an AICc bandwidth chosen by golden-section search (Fotheringham, Brunsdon and Charlton, Geographically Weighted Regression, 2002)
equivalents.GeneralizedLinearRegression: a generalized linear model fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares — Gaussian identity, binomial logit, Poisson log (McCullagh and Nelder, Generalized Linear Models, 2nd ed., 1989)
equivalents.GeographicallyWeightedRegression: geographically weighted regression with a Gaussian kernel, the bandwidth by golden-section search on AICc or cross-validation (Fotheringham, Brunsdon and Charlton, Geographically Weighted Regression, 2002)
equivalents.HotSpotAnalysisComparison: the spatial fuzzy kappa as its pages define it, the expected similarity's random pairings drawn with NumPy's PCG64 from env.randomGenerator (How Hot Spot Analysis Comparison works; Hagen-Zanker 2009, IJGIS 23:1, 61-73)

equivalents.MGWR: multiscale geographically weighted regression by back-fitting, a bandwidth per variable chosen on AICc (Fotheringham, Yang and Kang 2017; Oshan, Li, Kang, Wolf and Fotheringham 2019 (mgwr))

equivalents.OrdinaryLeastSquares: ordinary least squares with classical, White (HC0), Koenker–Bassett and Jarque–Bera diagnostics (Greene, Econometric Analysis, 7th ed., ch. 4–5 and 9; White 1980; Koenker 1981; Jarque and Bera 1980)
equivalents.PrepareData: random and nearest-neighbour test splits and the published balancing methods — random under- and oversampling, Tomek links, k-medoids undersampling, SMOTE and greedy spatial thinning — drawn with NumPy's PCG64 from env.randomGenerator (Tomek 1976; Chawla, Bowyer, Hall and Kegelmeyer 2002; Park and Jun 2009; Esri's "How Prepare Data for Prediction works")
equivalents.SAR: Anselin's LM tests and the documented model choice; the spatial lag model by spatial two-stage least squares, the error model by Kelejian and Prucha's generalized moments and feasible GLS, the combined model by generalized spatial two-stage least squares (Anselin 1988; Anselin, Bera, Florax and Yoon 1996; Kelejian and Prucha 1998, 1999)
equivalents.SpatiallyConstrainedMultivariateClusteri: SKATER — a minimum spanning tree of the neighbour graph cut where it most reduces the within-cluster sum of squares — with membership probabilities from SKATER rerun on random spanning trees, drawn with NumPy's PCG64 from env.randomGenerator (Assunção, Neves, Câmara and da Costa Freitas 2006; Calinski and Harabasz 1974; Esri's "How Spatially Constrained Multivariate Clustering works")
equivalents.TimeSeriesSmoothing: backward, forward and centered moving averages over a closed time window (Esri's "How Time Series Smoothing works"; Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd ed., §3.3)

equivalents.AddCompressionLayout: orthogonal-order-preserving compaction of the junction groups: each gap between successive group positions on x and on y shortened to the grouping distance (Misue, Eades, Lai and Sugiyama 1995, Layout Adjustment and the Mental Map)
equivalents.AddForceDirectedLayout: force-directed placement: repulsion k²/d between junctions, attraction d²/k along edges, a linearly cooling temperature (Fruchterman and Reingold 1991, Graph Drawing by Force-directed Placement)
equivalents.AddMainRingLayout: the main ring as the longest cycle found by depth-first search, junctions evenly round it, the rest as tidy trees outward (Reingold and Tilford 1981; Tarjan 1972, Depth-first search and linear graph algorithms)
equivalents.AddMainlineTreeLayout: the tidy tree drawing: each subtree pushed against its left neighbour along their contours, a parent centred over its first and last child (Reingold and Tilford 1981, Tidier Drawings of Trees)
equivalents.AddRadialTreeLayout: a radial tree: one concentric circle per level, each subtree given an angular wedge in proportion to its leaves (Eades 1992, Drawing free trees)
equivalents.AddSmartTreeLayout: the tidy tree drawing: each subtree pushed against its left neighbour along their contours, a parent centred over its first and last child (Reingold and Tilford 1981, Tidier Drawings of Trees)
equivalents.AddSpatialDispatchLayout: the force-scan: junctions nearer than the separation pushed apart along the line joining them (Misue, Eades, Lai and Sugiyama 1995, Layout Adjustment and the Mental Map)
